## 1. 8. Digital management practices > 8.12 Purchasing and contract management > 8.12.1 Procurement
Source: Government Functional Standard GovS 005: Digital (`govs-005`), Government Digital Service. Authority: mandatory. page last updated 2026-10-01.
Cite inline as: ([Government Functional Standard GovS 005: Digital: 8.12.1 Procurement](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/government-functional-standard-govs-005-digital/government-functional-standard-govs-005-digital-html#procurement))

Obligations in this section (verbatim, strength from the modal verb):
- [MANDATORY] "Organisations shall decide whether service solutions or components should be built internally, supplied by a third party, reused from existing government solutions, or delivered through a combination of approaches."
  - Possible conflict (machine-suggested, NOT verified): similar wording in "The Consultancy Playbook", pages about 4.1 years apart: "Even if previous knowledge does not answer all requirements, organisations should be asking themselves whether work that has previously been undertaken and the related outputs can inform the project brief and rationale." https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/631f2237e90e077db807dd00/The_Consultancy_Playbook_Version_1.1_September_2022.pdf#page=12
  - Possible conflict (machine-suggested, NOT verified): similar wording in "The Rose Book: guidance on knowledge asset management in government", pages about 2.5 years apart: "Therefore, organisations should consider whether or not the public interest is best served by controlling access to the asset." https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/knowledge-asset-management-in-government/knowledge-asset-management-strategies-what-to-include-and-where-to-start#box-6d-considering-social-economic-and-financial-value-when-exploiting-knowledge-assets
- [MANDATORY] "Government Functional Standard GovS 008: Commercial shall be complied with, with respect to procurement and management of contracts."
- [RECOMMENDED] "Purchasing strategies should support commercial, contractual, technology, data and AI considerations, including whether existing products or government solutions can meet the need."
- [RECOMMENDED] "Decisions should take account of insights and research and should reflect that, where possible, commercial off-the-shelf products or existing solutions already in use across government should be used."
  - Possible conflict (machine-suggested, NOT verified): similar wording in "The Digital, Data and Technology Playbook", pages about 3.3 years apart: "It takes you through the commercial lifecycle, identifying the key areas where decisions should be made, or action taken, on Intellectual property." https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/the-digital-data-and-technology-playbook/intellectual-property-rights-guidance-note-html#about-this-section-1
- [RECOMMENDED] "Building or tailoring a solution should only be considered where:"
- [RECOMMENDED] "An assessment of resources should be made to inform build or buy decisions, such as staff and funding, skills, operational capacity and the ability to deliver ongoing training."
- [RECOMMENDED] "Note: See Should Cost modelling for purchasing strategy guidance."

Section text (verbatim):
> Organisations shall decide whether service solutions or components should be built internally, supplied by a third party, reused from existing government solutions, or delivered through a combination of approaches.
> Purchasing strategies should support commercial, contractual, technology, data and AI considerations, including whether existing products or government solutions can meet the need.
> Decisions should take account of insights and research and should reflect that, where possible, commercial off-the-shelf products or existing solutions already in use across government should be used.
> Building or tailoring a solution should only be considered where:
> user need is unique or rare
> supplier options are limited
> commercial products cannot be scaled, adapted or assured to meet the need
> there are clear reasons to own, modify or control the technology, data or AI model
> An assessment of resources should be made to inform build or buy decisions, such as staff and funding, skills, operational capacity and the ability to deliver ongoing training.
> Government Functional Standard GovS 008: Commercial shall be complied with, with respect to procurement and management of contracts.
> Note: See Should Cost modelling for purchasing strategy guidance. [footnote 41]

## 2. 5. Service management > 5.3 Service design and development
Source: Government Functional Standard GovS 005: Digital (`govs-005`), Government Digital Service. Authority: mandatory. page last updated 2026-10-01.
Cite inline as: ([Government Functional Standard GovS 005: Digital: 5.3 Service design and development](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/government-functional-standard-govs-005-digital/government-functional-standard-govs-005-digital-html#service-design-and-development))

Obligations in this section (verbatim, strength from the modal verb):
- [MANDATORY] "Services shall be delivered in accordance with the Service Standard."
  - Possible conflict (machine-suggested, NOT verified): similar wording in "Service Manual", pages about 1.2 years apart: "COTS products and services must be designed to meet the specific needs of the users of your service." https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/technology/commercial-off-the-shelf-products-and-services#user-centred-design
- [MANDATORY] "Services shall be monitored using consistent service performance measures (see 5.6), reviewed quarterly."
